prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Predictions continue to underpredict gains on winning tests while remaining overoptimistic for non-winning tests.
Sign-in hint (6 of 12 tests) and home wait_info (4 of 8 tests) changes were helpful.

Sign-in reorder changes consistently reduced performance across 2 tests.
Choose_path copy, choose_path layout, home redesign, adoption redesign, adoption incentive, and home new_screen changes showed no clear effect across multiple tests.
Evidence remains thin for change types tested only once.

Changes:
0: [sign_in, hint] Sign-In Pet Profile Sync Assurance Hint: Displays a clear sign-in reassurance hint explaining that signing in binds and protects pet profile data to cloud account credentials. (why: Support received 8 emails regarding missing or reset pets after signing in again, and sign-in hints have historically won 50% of tests.)
1: [home, wait_info] Desktop Pet Rendering Stage Step Counter Display: Enables an explicit step counter on the waiting screen to show active rendering progress stages. (why: Home waiting step has a long mean duration (2336s) and high drop-off; wait_info changes on home have won 4 out of 8 previous tests.)
2: [finish, new_flow] Desktop Companion System Tray Control Flow: Adds an interactive flow component to the finish screen explaining system tray desktop pet controls. (why: Support received 3 emails from users confused about how to hide, control, or talk to their pet after onboarding. Finish step new_flow changes have won 2 of 6 past tests.)
3: [choose_path, redesign] Choose Path Story Compact Stage Redesign: Redesigns the choose path step into a structured stage layout showcasing path selection cleanly. (why: Choose path drops 20.3% of users with an 8s median / 514s mean time. A stage layout provides a clear visual structure for path selection.)
4: [adoption, redesign] Adoption Certificate Official Seal Card Redesign: Redesigns the adoption certificate screen into a card layout with dedicated verification elements. (why: Adoption stage experiences the largest conversion drop (66.0% completion rate). Redesigning the certificate card increases user emotional commitment.)
5: [finish, new_screen] Desktop Pet Quick Actions Guide Screen: Adds a dedicated post-onboarding guide screen explaining how to summon, hide, and interact with the pet on desktop. (why: Addresses post-onboarding support complaints (3 emails) regarding lack of clarity on how to control or hide the desktop companion.)
6: [sign_in, hint] Sign-In Cloud Account Recovery Protection Hint: Adds a sign-in hint emphasizing multi-session recovery safety and account state persistence. (why: Directly targets 8 support complaints about missing or reset pets post sign-in while capitalizing on effective sign-in hint patterns.)
7: [home, wait_info] Desktop Pet Rendering Asset Download Progress Display: Displays an active asset generation progress bar during the rendering wait step. (why: The home wait stage takes 201s median / 2336s mean. Providing active progress info reduces drop-off during long renders.)
8: [finish, redesign] Home Intro Companion Desktop Setup Stage Redesign: Redesigns the final finish screen into a focal stage layout highlighting pet desktop activation. (why: Finish screen conversion currently drops 20% (80.1%). A clear stage redesign builds completion momentum as the pet launches.)
9: [adoption, notification] Custom Pet Upload Generation Notification Switch: Enables desktop readiness notifications on photo upload so users are notified if pet rendering takes extra time. (why: Support received 3 emails about custom pet photo making stalling or failing, while adoption drops off at 66.0%.)
